best_for: Firefox users who want workspaces, split view and a web-panel sidebar built in, without a pile of extensions or a Mozilla account.
description:
Floorp is a web browser built on Firefox. It is made by the Floorp Projects together with Ablaze, a software community that started in Japan.

You can set tabs out the way you like: in a bar across the top, in a vertical list or in several rows. Mouse gestures let you go back, go forward or reload by holding the right button and drawing a short line, and you can make your own gestures. You can also open a site in its own window as a web app, set your own keyboard shortcuts, find any command from a command palette, and change the theme and other parts of the interface.

points.title: Firefox underneath, kept current
points.text: Floorp follows Firefox releases rather than an extended-support base. Version 12.21.0 moved to the Firefox 159 series.

points.title: Built-in layout tools
points.text: Workspaces group tabs by task and can use Firefox containers to keep logins apart. Split view puts up to four pages in one window, and the sidebar holds pinned sites, notes and tools.

points.title: Telemetry is off by default
points.text: Mozilla telemetry and health reports are switched off out of the box, and Mozilla's sponsored shortcuts were turned off by default from 12.21.1. Shortcut and web-panel icons are fetched from Google's favicon service, which sees the site address.

points.title: Workspace sync with limits
points.text: Since 12.21.0 you can sync chosen workspaces and their tabs through a Mozilla Account. Private windows, local files, cookies and container assignments do not travel.

points.title: No account to start
points.text: Floorp runs without any sign-in and has a built-in tool to import data from another browser. It is open source under the MPL 2.0 and accepts donations.

points.title: Platforms and builds
points.text: Windows needs 10 or 11 and installs for the whole machine. The Mac build is universal and runs on macOS 10.15 or later. On Linux, the Flatpak listed here is verified on Flathub as published by Ablaze, for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Version numbers drift by platform
points.text: Releases land on different days per platform, so Windows, Mac and Linux can show different point versions. The Windows listing keeps 50 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
